documents.unit: AI at Boise State (Student Use of AI)
documents.title: AI in Learning
documents.summary: Short student-facing page. It says instructors decide AI use course by course, promotes the university platform and a literacy course, and warns about personal data and documenting prompts.
documents.stance_why: The page says "instructors generally determine generative AI use classroom guidelines on a case-by-case basis" and sets no university-wide rule, so it delegates.

units.why: The sentence says "instructors generally determine generative AI use classroom guidelines on a case-by-case basis", so the university sets no rule and hands the decision to instructors: P04, not P05 since no tiers are named.
units.anchor: Boise State instructors generally determine generative AI use classroom guidelines on a case-by-case basis.

units.why: "Always check with your instructor" tells students to confirm expectations rather than assume; this fits P10 (ask first) rather than P04 because it is addressed to the student and prescribes an action.
units.anchor: Always check with your instructor to ensure you have a solid understanding of their expectations.

units.why: The page states the university wants students to "develop practical and professional generative AI skills", a career-preparation rationale (P44), not a rule on use.
units.anchor: We want you to develop practical and professional generative AI skills

units.why: The page offers the "university-built generative AI platform boisestate.ai" for students "when permissible", which is a sanctioned institutional tool (P17).
units.anchor: university-built generative AI platform boisestate.ai

units.why: The "AI Literacy And Student Success" online course "familiarizes you with generative AI tools and how to use them responsibly", teaching AI use as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: familiarizes you with generative AI tools and how to use them responsibly

units.why: "avoid entering personally identifiable information, confidential, sensitive, private, restricted data" is a data-protection rule even for authorized use (P50).
units.anchor: avoid entering personally identifiable information, confidential, sensitive, private, restricted data
units.frag_start: Even if your use of AI

units.why: The page tells students to "ensure generated content is lawful"; this is a legal-compliance expectation that fits no type (not P52 copyright, not P53 harms), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: ensure generated content is lawful
units.frag_end: is lawful and carefully document your prompts and iterations
units.uncovered_note: Students should prompt so that AI-generated content is lawful.

units.why: Students should "carefully document your prompts and iterations" so their own ideas are distinguishable from AI ones; this is keeping prompt records (P26), not a per-submission disclosure statement (P24).
units.anchor: carefully document your prompts and iterations to ensure you retain your voice
units.frag_start: carefully document your prompts and iterations

units.why: The Strategic Plan "values technological and educational innovation and excellence" and "honesty and the responsible use", an institution-level statement of principles (P56).
units.anchor: institutional values developed and endorsed by faculty, staff, and leaders on campus
units.frag_start: Generative AI Strategic Plan lays out

documents.title: An approach to discussing AI in your department
documents.summary: A CS department news post summarizing a faculty committee process. It presents five integration scenarios, a re-weighted assessment approach for lower-division courses, and a CS 321 pilot plan. It is advice, not a binding rule.
documents.stance_why: The post lays out five scenarios (No, Restricted, Guided, Open, Full GenAI) and assigns them per course ("which scenario fit best for each course"), so it offers tiers and does not set one department stance.

units.why: The post says the challenge is "to help CS students learn the fundamental concepts of CS without relying on AI", putting fundamentals first (P42).
units.anchor: help CS students learn the fundamental concepts of CS without relying on AI
units.frag_start: The challenge is to help CS students
units.frag_end: expects them to use AI tools.

units.why: The same passage says students then use AI "to prepare them for a workforce that expects them to use AI tools", a career rationale (P44).
units.anchor: prepare them for a workforce that expects them to use AI tools
units.frag_start: The challenge is to help CS students
units.frag_end: expects them to use AI tools.

units.why: The committee "recommends that the department should create a student-facing summary document" explaining rationale; it is a communication-of-expectations step (P09 closest).
units.anchor: create a student-facing summary document that explains the rationale for the upcoming GenAI integration
units.frag_start: The committee recommends that the department

units.why: The committee recommends "a short blurb that can be included in syllabi with a link to the summary document", a syllabus AI statement (P09).
units.anchor: developing a short blurb that can be included in syllabi
units.frag_start: We also recommend developing a short blurb

units.why: The committee "strongly encourage[s] faculty members to experiment and gain experience with various AI tools", i.e. support for faculty learning AI (P63).
units.anchor: strongly encourage faculty members to experiment and gain experience with various AI tools
units.frag_start: The committee emphasizes that the department should

units.why: "10-15 minute mini-workshops in department meetings" are a faculty professional development suggestion (P63), distinct from the encouragement to experiment.
units.anchor: holding 10-15 minute mini-workshops in department meetings where one tool or technique is demonstrated

units.why: "fundamental courses prioritize fundamental skill development" names skills that students must demonstrate individually, a fundamentals-first rationale (P42).
units.anchor: fundamental courses prioritize fundamental skill development
units.frag_start: In Computer Science, fundamental courses prioritize

units.why: The list of "new AI skills (prompt engineering, critical evaluation and verification of AI-generated code ...)" states what the department wants taught about AI, a professional-skills goal (P44).
units.anchor: new AI skills (prompt engineering, critical evaluation and verification of AI-generated code
units.frag_start: In order to better prepare students for the workforce

units.why: Departments "should consider what changes need to be made to their courses without sacrificing program or course outcomes", a planning principle for other units (P56).
units.anchor: Departments should consider what changes need to be made to their courses

units.why: The committee "broke down potential scenarios into 5 different integration scenarios" ranging from No GenAI to Full Integration: named levels of use (P05).
units.anchor: broke down potential scenarios into 5 different integration
units.frag_start: To help determine how AI could be integrated

units.why: Each course is matched to a scenario ("which scenario fit best for each course"), so the rule is set per course rather than department-wide (P04).
units.anchor: determine which scenario fit best for each course
units.frag_start: The committee then discussed a selection of courses

units.why: Scenario 1 says "Students develop core competencies without AI assistance", a no-AI default for that scenario (P01).
units.anchor: Students develop core competencies without AI assistance.

units.why: "GenAI use constitutes academic dishonesty" classifies use in Scenario 1 as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: GenAI use constitutes academic dishonesty.

units.why: Scenario 2 permits AI "only for specific, instructor-defined tasks (e.g., explaining error messages, suggesting debugging approaches)", the error-help use (P13); the restriction to listed tasks makes it restrict.
units.anchor: explaining error messages, suggesting debugging approaches
units.frag_start: GenAI is permitted only for specific

units.why: "Prohibited for code generation" bans AI-written code in Scenario 2 (P19).
units.anchor: Prohibited for code generation.

units.why: "Students must document AI interactions" in Scenario 2 requires keeping a record of AI use (P26); it is not a citation format so not P25.
units.anchor: Students must document AI interactions.

units.why: Scenario 3 requires that "Students must verify, understand, and modify all AI-generated code"; verification of AI output (P31) is the lead duty, understanding (P30) is secondary.
units.anchor: Students must verify, understand, and modify all AI-generated code.

units.why: "Emphasis on prompt engineering and output validation as learning objectives" makes AI skill itself a course goal (P44).
units.anchor: Emphasis on prompt engineering and output validation as learning objectives.

units.why: Scenario 4 says "Students freely use GenAI", i.e. open permission by default (P02).
units.anchor: Students freely use GenAI but must demonstrate understanding

units.why: "Assessments focus on comprehension and application rather than initial code creation" redesigns assessment around AI (P35).
units.anchor: Assessments focus on comprehension and application rather than initial code creation.

units.why: Scenario 5 says "GenAI usage mirrors professional practice", full integration of AI (P02).
units.anchor: GenAI usage mirrors professional practice.

units.why: Students are "evaluated on problem decomposition, tool selection, and quality assurance rather than manual coding", a redesign of grading around AI (P35).
units.anchor: evaluated on problem decomposition, tool selection, and quality assurance rather than manual coding

units.why: For lower-division courses "where AI use is discouraged", AI is discouraged but the scenario is not a formal ban (P03).
units.anchor: For lower division courses where AI use is discouraged
units.frag_start: For lower division courses where AI use is discouraged

units.why: The quoted recommendation "it is a losing battle to prevent AI use" shows staff relying on assessment redesign instead of policing use (P60).
units.anchor: recognize it is a losing battle to prevent AI use
units.frag_start: recognize it is a losing battle

units.why: "assessments must be re-weighted and redesigned to make AI code generation without understanding a detriment to success" is a redesign of assessments around AI (P35).
units.anchor: assessments must be re-weighted and redesigned to make AI code generation without understanding a detriment

units.why: "at least half of all course points will come from demonstration of understanding through paper or proctored quizzes and exams without access to AI" shifts weight to unassisted assessment (P33, which also implies P22 but states a weighting).
units.anchor: at least half of all course points will come from demonstration of understanding
units.frag_start: Instead, at least half of all course points

units.why: "Producing working code, alone, will not be adequate to receive a passing grade" changes grading criteria because of AI (P35).
units.anchor: Producing working code, alone, will not be adequate to receive a passing grade

units.why: "Programming assignments, then, are framed as learning and practice exercises to prepare for quizzes and exams" redesigns the role of assignments (P35).
units.anchor: Programming assignments, then, are framed as learning and practice exercises

units.why: Homework programming "may shift away from producing functioning code ... toward code comprehension, exploration, analysis, debugging" redesigns assignments (P35).
units.anchor: toward code comprehension, exploration, analysis, debugging, and comparison of alternative solutions
units.frag_start: The focus of in-class and formative homework-level

units.why: For CS 321 the committee says GenAI "would be used in S2 mode for the first individual projects and then students would transition to S3 mode", permission staged as skills develop (P08).
units.anchor: GenAI would be used in S2 mode for the first individual projects
units.frag_start: For projects, GenAI would be used in S2 mode

units.why: CS 321 should keep "continuing to restrict it for foundational computer science concepts", a fundamentals-first rule (P42).
units.anchor: continuing to restrict it for foundational computer science concepts

units.why: The CS 321 plan to "Change all exams to be in-class" moves weight to unassisted assessment (P33).
units.anchor: Change all exams to be in-class.

units.why: "Add some form of interactive assessment for projects" checks understanding through live interaction (P34).
units.anchor: Add some form of interactive assessment for projects
units.frag_start: Add some form of interactive assessment

units.why: A "custom NotebookLM with all class notes, code examples, and project writeups" is a course-specific AI study tool (P17).
units.anchor: Use a custom NotebookLM with all class notes, code examples, and project writeups
units.frag_start: Use a custom NotebookLM with all class notes

units.why: Having students "find a flaw! (or hallucinations)" in AI output teaches verification of AI output (P31).
units.anchor: find a flaw! (or hallucinations).
units.frag_start: Ask students to hear the overview podcast

units.why: "Students use CoPilot in ask/edit mode for p1, p2, and p3" prescribes an IDE-integrated AI assistant in a set mode (P07, not P17 since Copilot is not course-built).
units.anchor: Students use CoPilot in ask/edit mode for p1, p2, and p3.
units.frag_start: Students use CoPilot in ask/edit mode

units.why: "Students will include a log of interactions and a reflection for each project" requires logs and reflections (P26).
units.anchor: Students will include a log of interactions and a reflection for each project.

units.why: An "AI warmup project" before project 4 is a planned activity that teaches AI use (P44).
units.anchor: Create AI warmup project to be used before project 4
units.frag_start: Create AI warmup project to be used

units.why: "Add AI exploration topics in each chapter" builds AI content into the course (P44).
units.anchor: Add AI exploration topics in each chapter.

units.why: The S2 tutor prompt says "You are a tutoring system and not allowed to provide full code for any of the included projects", setting AI as a hint-giving tutor (P12).
units.anchor: You are a tutoring system and not allowed to provide full code
units.frag_start: You are a tutoring system and not allowed

notes: Coder B. Only the two included documents were coded. S2/S3 in CS 321 refer to Scenarios 2 and 3. One UNCOVERED unit (lawful content).
